steps.area: The number of buildings and the project area give the building density in buildings per hectare. Unless you enter a network length, the tool estimates the length from this density. The number of buildings also sets the heat pump investment and the connection fees.
steps.buildings: The shares split the buildings into types and construction periods. Each group gets the default heating demand, cooling demand and floor area of Tables 1 to 3; together they give the total annual demand. Industry has no default values: it adds no demand and leads to “Further analysis required”.
steps.sources: Each selected source adds the default annual capacity of its potential (Tables 4 and 5). The heat pump turns it into delivered heating and cooling, which sets the coverage, the installation costs and the electricity costs. A source with unknown potential adds nothing and leads to “Further analysis required”.
steps.options: A known heating or cooling demand replaces the estimated total, and a known network length replaces the estimated length. PV lowers the electricity costs of the heat pumps by the PV cost reduction of Table 6.
steps.assumptions: A changed parameter replaces the default of Tables 4 to 6 in every equation that uses it. Results then carry the “Custom parameters” badge.

heatingDemandKwh.text: The buildings of each type and construction period times their default heating demand per m² and their default floor area, summed over all groups.
heatingDemandKwh.manual: You entered the total heating demand, so it replaces the estimate.

coolingDemandKwh.text: The buildings of each type and construction period times their default cooling demand per m² and their default floor area, summed over all groups.
coolingDemandKwh.manual: You entered the total cooling demand, so it replaces the estimate.

buildingDensity.text: The number of buildings per hectare of project area.

densityCategory.text: Follows from the building density class of Table 8: low density is rural, medium is sub-urban, high is urban.

specificNetworkLength.text: Network metres per hectare, estimated from the building density with the predefined relationship of the methodology.

networkLengthM.text: The specific network length times the project area in hectares.
networkLengthM.manual: You entered the network length, so it replaces the estimate.

heatDensityMwhPerM.text: The total heating demand divided by the network length. It is classified in MWh per metre (Table 9).

heatingSupplyKwh.text: For each selected source, the default capacity of its potential plus the share the heat pump adds (COP), summed over all sources. Solar thermal works without a heat pump.

coolingSupplyKwh.text: For each selected source, the default cooling capacity of its potential adjusted by the COP, summed over all sources. Waste heat and solar thermal supply no cooling.

heatingCoverage.text: The heating supply divided by the heating demand: the share of the annual heating demand the selected sources can cover.

coolingCoverage.text: The cooling supply divided by the cooling demand: the share of the annual cooling demand the selected sources can cover.

chRatio.text: The smaller of the heating and cooling demand divided by the larger one. The closer it is to one, the more balanced the demands.

heatingRevenue.text: The heating base price for every m² of floor area per year, plus the heating energy price for every kWh of heating demand.

coolingRevenue.text: The cooling base price for every m² of floor area per year, plus the cooling energy price for every kWh of cooling demand.

connectionFeeRevenue.text: The one-time connection fee of every building, spread over the depreciation period with the annuity factor.

overallRevenue.text: Heating revenue, cooling revenue and the annualized connection fees.

networkInvestment.text: The network construction costs per metre times the network length.

supplyInvestment.text: For each selected source, its installation costs per kWh/a times its heating supply, summed over all sources. Ambient air adds no installation costs, as the heat pumps are counted separately.

heatPumpInvestment.text: The investment in one heat pump times the number of buildings.

overallInvestment.text: Heat pumps, network and the installations of all sources. The installations are counted once.

annuityFactor.text: Turns an investment into equal yearly payments over the depreciation period at the interest rate.

annualizedCosts.text: The overall investment times the annuity factor: its cost per year.

electricityCosts.text: The electricity the heat pumps need (supply divided by COP) times the electricity price. With PV, the costs are lowered by the PV cost reduction.

operationAndMaintenance.text: A fixed share of the overall investment every year.

annualCosts.text: Annualized investment, electricity costs, and operation and maintenance costs.

economicRatio.text: The overall revenues divided by the annual costs. The economic assessment rates this ratio as favorable, unclear or clearly unfavorable.

level.text: The overall result combines the supply coverage, the building and heat density and the economic assessment (Table 11). Industry in the project area or a source with unknown potential always leads to “Further analysis required”.

formulas.eq-03-01: Number of buildings per type and construction period
formulas.eq-03-02a: Annual heating demand per building group
formulas.eq-03-02b: Annual cooling demand per building group

ui.title: How we calculate
ui.noEquation: The methodology gives no equation for this value; the resolved answer that follows is used.
